reapack.name: ReaKit FX
reapack.desc: ReaKit FX - GainKit, Saturation, 3-Band EQ, DDC, De-Esser and Stereo Width: free effects with EON Studios interfaces (the ReaKit library)

metadata.description: Six free effects with EON Studios interfaces. Saturation, 3-Band EQ and DDC (Digital Drum Compressor) by Michael Gruhn (LOSER) and a De-Esser built on Lubomir I. Ivanov's (Liteon), free as their authors released them, with their original terms and credits (LICENSE.md); and EON's own GainKit (gain staging on a VU, one meter or two) and Stereo Width (MIT). The shared interface library that comes with them is ReaKit (MIT).

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: First release: Saturation, 3-Band EQ, DDC and De-Esser, with EON Studios interfaces. Free, as LOSER and Liteon released them, and credited in each plugin.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: The THEME panel gains a NAME BAR row: per instance, show or hide REAPER's own name bar over the plugin's mixer-strip and track-panel embed (hidden by default, as before). A click on the strip closes the plugin's floating window. Digits under 10 px draw regular (bold Arial at 8 and 9 px turns a 5 into a 6), in the plugins and in the link badge. The panel's KNOB chip names the knob actually on screen. 3-Band EQ: the standalone window draws everything at one scale that follows the window, and in a wide, short window the readouts stay clear of the legend.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: The effects have their own repository now; this is the same package, continued. New: GainKit, EON's gain-staging plugin -- an analog VU (the ReaKit meter), one GAIN knob and a STEREO / MONO key, with a mixer-strip face that shows the VU over the knob, the VU alone or the knob alone, its numerals or ticks only, and a VU that grows flatter as the strip is dragged wider; a name you type on the meter's face; hidden HP / LP filters, trims and M/S kept as parameters for old projects. Every plugin's shared includes match ReaKit 1.7.0.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: De-Esser: no more pop when playback starts or when the effect is enabled while sound is already flowing through it (input monitoring, the enable button during playback). REAPER re-runs a JSFX's @init on those events, and the De-Esser's @init cleared its lookahead buffer, its crossover states and its detector -- a millisecond of silence and the filters restarting from nothing. It initialises once now and re-takes its rate-derived values from @block when the sample rate changes. Measured before and after in a sandbox: the largest one-sample step on play start went from 11 times the test tone's own slope to the slope itself.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: DDC: the Mix knob blends the compressed signal with a dry of the same moment. The dry used to be taken before the lookahead and the oversampler, and the wet left them a few milliseconds later, so any Mix under 100 % with lookahead on was a comb filter: measured in a sandbox, a 100 Hz tone at 50 % Mix with 5 ms lookahead came out at a two-hundredth of its level; it comes out whole now. De-Esser: the normal output is no longer clamped at 0 dBFS (an undocumented limiter in REAPER's floating-point chain: a signal peaking at 2.0 came out at 1.0, now 2.0); the sidechain-monitor output keeps its clamp.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: Saturation: no more clicks on hot transients. The curve clamped its input and its output at 0 dBFS, so in REAPER's floating-point chain anything louder was brick-wall clipped however low the Drive -- a clipped drum hit is a loud click. The curve now saturates onto its own peak, smoothly, and the output may run past 0 dBFS the way the chain allows: at Drive 10 % a signal peaking at 2.0 used to come out at 1.0 and now comes out at 1.98; at Drive 100 % the peak is exactly 1.0, as before. Also initialises once, so a knob being dragged when playback starts keeps its drag.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: 3-Band EQ, Saturation, De-Esser: NATIVE on the THEME panel now means native. It used to turn only the knob and button colours native while the background, the text and the knob style stayed themed, and the choice was forgotten when the project reloaded. Each plugin now gates its theming the way GainKit does and keeps the NATIVE pick on a hidden parameter, so it comes back with the project.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: GainKit 2.3.0. In a mixer strip the meter itself is the gain control: drag it up or down (Ctrl fine, Shift finer), the wheel steps it, double-click or right-click returns it to 0 dB, and the value shows under a VU-only meter for a moment; the rest of the strip still opens the window with a click. The THEME panel gains a FONT row: the face the name is printed in, on the window's meter and under the strip's (Arial, Arial Black, Impact, Georgia, Times New Roman, Courier New, Consolas, Verdana, Segoe UI). GainKit Plus: with the GainKit Plus script running (its own package in this repository), every GainKit shows its track's name as the meter's legend, the track's colour as a thin bar along the top of the strip and under the window's header, and the track's icon in the window's header; a name typed on the meter still wins. Without the script nothing changes.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: GainKit 2.5.0. The name sits on top of the mixer strip in every view (the VU over the knob, the knob alone, the VU alone): as a plain row, on a band in the track's colour, or not at all (THEME panel: NAME). The VU alone gets its own STEREO / MONO key under the name, shows the gain as a tint of the meter's face (up from the middle for a boost, down for a cut), and prints the value under the meter while you set it or all the time (THEME panel: VALUE). The meter can take the track's colour, in the strip and in the window (THEME panel: VU COLOR). The name is the one typed on the meter or the track's, and the colour the track's, from the GainKit Plus script. DDC: 2x now oversamples only the detector, so it follows the peaks between samples while the audio stays at the project's rate: 2x keeps the top end (it used to take about 2 to 3 dB off at 15 kHz and 5 to 6 dB at 20 kHz) and adds no latency, and with 2x off DDC sounds exactly as before. Its gain-reduction meter is updated once per block instead of on every sample. De-Esser: the Target and Monitor switches take effect between audio blocks. The meter and the switches change no sound.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: DDC: the Attack knob now means what it says. The gain reduction is applied as it is computed, as in LOSER's original; a 10 ms smoother after it had made every attack under about 10 ms sound the same, so mixes that use DDC with a fast attack will sound punchier. Moving a control with 2x on no longer upsets the detector for a moment. De-Esser: in a project below 40 kHz (32 or 22.05 kHz) a high Frequency could push the crossover past what the sample rate can hold and the filter blew up; its edges now stay below that limit, and nothing changes at 44.1 kHz and above. GainKit 2.5.1: the master's GainKit shows the project's name (from GainKit Plus 1.0.4). DDC and the De-Esser carry their authors' full original headers again; the De-Esser is under the GPL, as Liteon released it.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: GainKit 2.6.0: on REAPER 7.81 and later every GainKit shows its track's name by itself, read from REAPER, with no script running; on an older REAPER the name still comes from GainKit Plus, and the colour, the icon and the master's project name come from GainKit Plus on every version. A name typed on the meter still wins. A long name shortened with ".." is never cut in the middle of an accented letter. DDC: the lookahead reaches its full 5 ms at every sample rate up to 409.6 kHz (it stopped at 2.7 ms at 384 kHz); below 204.8 kHz nothing changes, measured sample for sample at 48 and 44.1 kHz.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: Link groups: a project opened in a freshly started REAPER with a plugin set to a link group used to take the group's empty values for every control still at its default (GainKit's HP came back at 0 Hz, its LP at 0 Hz); the first plugin to wake now fills the group with its own saved settings, and the controls you had moved were never affected. Saturation and 3-Band EQ: the Play / Record / Stop processing options in their menus now do what they say (they used to gate only the meter, or nothing); with the options at their defaults, all on, nothing changes. De-Esser: with one of those options off, the sound still passes through the lookahead delay, so the track stays in time with the rest. GainKit 2.6.1 tells REAPER it has a settling tail (its filters), as the other plugins do.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: New: Stereo Width, EON's own mid/side width control, free. One knob from mono through the recorded width to twice as wide; it scales the side signal and leaves the centre where it is, with a correlation meter under the knob. In a mixer strip it is the WIDTH knob at the bottom of the channel, so the free set now makes a complete strip: GainKit, Saturation, 3-Band EQ, DDC or the De-Esser, and Width, all in the theme and linkable.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: Themes without Swing. Three colour themes are built into the plugins now: EON, Dark and Light. Pick one on any of the six and all six follow, the knob styles too, and the choice comes back with the project. Until now the THEME menu only asked Swing's bridge for a theme, so on a machine without Swing nothing happened; now the plugins paint those three themselves. The other eleven themes in the list are marked "Swing" and light up when EON Swing is installed. The six also share one memory space (one pick reaches them all), and their link-group bands moved out of a range Swing uses, so link groups re-seed once from each instance's own settings.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: Without Swing, a theme change lands at once. 1.4.0 waited a third of a second for a bridge before painting the theme itself, so wheeling through EON, Dark and Light felt slow; the wait is now a few frames, still long enough for Swing's bridge to answer first when it is there.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: 3-Band EQ 1.3.0: the mixer strip is three times taller, with the rows refitted so every value sits clear of its label (drag the strip taller and the faces grow with it). The wheel over the THEME panel's KNOB chip steps one style per tick again, without Swing too.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: Opening a project wears the theme it was saved with, over whatever the previous project left in place (without Swing).

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: EON is the default look. On a machine without Swing, with no theme ever picked, the six now open on the EON theme instead of each plugin's bare colours. Pick another and it is remembered as before.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: Without Swing, the THEME list shows only what it can set: NATIVE, EON, Dark and Light. The eleven themes Swing's bridge paints appear in the list when EON Swing is installed.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: In the mixer strip and the track panel: double-click resets a knob again (an embedded plugin sees the mouse later and less often than a window, so its double-click window is wider now), and the link badge on the 3-Band EQ, Saturation, De-Esser and Stereo Width cycles the group when clicked instead of opening the window.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: No clicks: Saturation no longer pops when its window opens; DDC no longer clicks when you press play; GainKit, the 3-Band EQ, Saturation and Stereo Width ease in when inserted with their settings, and the Play/Rec/Stop toggles fade instead of switching in one sample (Stereo Width's knob and Enable glide too; its DC blocker is gone, so 100 % is an exact pass-through). Mixer strips that are not changing skip their redraw, so a big session stays quick (set REAPER's meter refresh to 120 for the snappiest strips). In the THEME panel, the wheel over the open theme or knob list steps through it. Less work per sample in DDC (RMS off), GainKit and the De-Esser.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: GainKit changes theme on its own: a session with only GainKits opens on EON and follows a pick on its THEME panel (until now it needed one of the other five open to do it), and double-click resets its meter in the mixer strip the way it does on the other five.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: NATIVE is for all six: picking NATIVE or a theme on any of them switches every one, open or closed, and a project opens the way it was saved. A new EMBED row on the THEME panel (MCP / TCP / OFF) shows the plugin in the mixer strip, in the track panel or in neither, and new copies of all six open there too (GainKit Plus does the moving; the row says NEEDS PLUS while it is not running). DDC has a THEME panel now. Cleaner windows: the THEME button sits in each header, and the credit line, the tips line and the "ReaKit" label are gone, their room given to the controls.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: Link groups forget plugins that are gone. A plugin that joins a group, or loads with one, now waits a moment to see whether any member is still running. It takes the group's settings only if one is; otherwise the group starts from its own. Deleting a group's plugins or closing their project no longer leaves its settings behind for the next plugin, and two projects open in tabs keep their own. DDC: moving Lookahead while audio plays no longer drops the sound out; the change glides over 10 ms, and moving Mix, Output or Link no longer cuts a long Hold short. 3-Band EQ: its crossover points glide when automated instead of stepping. GainKit and the De-Esser keep their short after-stop time the same length when the sample rate changes. GainKit's meter reads the louder side: a sound panned hard to one side, or two sides out of phase, now read at their real level instead of 6 dB low or not at all. A new METERS row on GainKit's THEME panel shows a meter for each side when set to TWO: in the window, side by side under the name, with a trim knob for each side and the rest of the window its usual size (a wider window, bigger meters), and in the strip, side by side (over the knob in the METER view). One needle stays the default. Two more rows: VU DRAG lets the strip's meter set the gain (drag it or turn the wheel over it, double-click for 0 dB) and shows the gain as a fill in the VU view. It is off by default, so a strip's meter now only reads until you turn it on. ST/MONO hides the STEREO / MONO key in the strip; MONO still shows, as a small cyan dot. GainKit's THEME panel now has two pages, LOOK and STRIP, with a line at the bottom saying what the row under the mouse does, so it fits a short window at full size. An idle mixer strip no longer misses several settings changed at once, as "Copy look to all" changes them.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: Link groups work in a render started straight after a project opens: the render queue, a command-line render, or opening a project and rendering at once. Automation on one linked plugin now moves the others in the rendered file. A plugin joining a group waits a moment to see whether the group is already running, and that moment now counts the audio being rendered as well as the time passing, so a fast render links the same way playback does. De-Esser: moving Lookahead no longer clicks. It glides to the new setting over 10 ms, as DDC's does. De-Esser: Monitor plays the band as late as the latency the plugin reports, so it lines up with the rest of the mix, and turning Monitor off carries on smoothly. GainKit: track names and icons with letters such as ü, é or € come through GainKit Plus whole, and an icon in a folder with such a letter in its name loads. That includes REAPER's own icons when your Windows user folder has one. Needs GainKit Plus 1.0.12.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: De-Esser: the spectrum shows the real frequency bands only, so its lowest and highest bars no longer pick up stray values. It looks at the left and right sides separately, so sound that is out of phase between them shows up instead of cancelling out of the picture, and it starts at the bottom of the graph instead of flashing full height. Display only: the sound is unchanged.

reapack.name: GainKit Plus.lua
reapack.desc: GainKit Plus - the track's name and colour on every GainKit's meter, and the actions that handle every GainKit at once

metadata.description: Companion scripts for GainKit (ReaKit FX). GainKit Plus, a background action, feeds every GainKit its track's name, colour and icon (the master's gets the project's name), and can start with REAPER. The others act on the GainKits in the project, FX containers included: Insert on selected tracks, GainKit first in every chain, GainKit first on selected tracks, GainKit last on the master, Copy look to all, Reset all gains, All MONO, All STEREO, Bypass all and Remove all GainKits; and ReaKit FX - Start with REAPER, one press that starts GainKit Plus and EON Floatter with REAPER. MIT, EON Studios.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: First release. GainKit Plus (a toggle: run it to start, run it again to stop) feeds every GainKit in the project its track's name, colour and icon while it runs. Six more actions: Insert on selected tracks (GainKit first in the chain of every selected track that has none), GainKit first in every chain (moves the GainKit a track already has to the top, the master's too), Reset all gains (every GainKit's GAIN to 0 dB), All MONO and All STEREO (every GainKit's key at once) and Bypass all (all off; again, all on). Each is one undo step. Needs GainKit 2.3.0 (ReaKit FX 1.2.0).

Nothing else in that file is touched. The toolbar button shows the state. Also: starting GainKit Plus right after stopping it is a start again (it used to read as a second stop for a second).

Bypass all's description says what it does: it bypasses every GainKit, and run again with all of them bypassed, it enables them all.

The master's GainKit shows the project's name (needs GainKit 2.5.1, ReaKit FX 1.2.2). The actions, and the names and colours, now reach a GainKit inside an FX container. Reset all gains resets only the GAIN: it used to set the THEME panel's VALUE row back to TOUCH as well.

reapack.name: EON_Floatter.lua
reapack.desc: EON Floatter - JSFX floating windows open at the size you chose

metadata.description:
EON Floatter opens every EON plugin's floating window at the size EON designed for it, and lets you keep your own size for any JSFX. Run it once: it switches on, starts with REAPER from then on, and shows its panel. Run it again to open the panel. Closing the panel never stops it.
The panel: every plugin drawn to scale against its default, Capture to keep a size as yours, Reset to go back to EON's, a live handle that resizes the real window, one dial for all EON sizes (75 to 150 percent for small laptops and big screens), and "Apply EON sizes to this project".
Needs js_ReaScriptAPI (ReaTeam Extensions). The panel needs ReaImGui; without it the sizing still works. MIT licensed.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: Floatter now also ships from the ReaKit FX repository, so the one import gives the plugins, GainKit Plus and the windows at their designed size. The same 1.0.1 as in the ReaKit library; installing both is harmless, only one ever runs. Needs js_ReaScriptAPI; the panel needs ReaImGui (both from ReaTeam Extensions).

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: A window you resize by hand keeps that size until REAPER closes, that window only; Floatter's own sizing (an apply, Capture, the dial) ends the keep. The 3-Band EQ's designed size follows its taller strip. The start-up file handling is hardened: a stranded original is put back before anything reads or writes, a block is removed in whole lines so a neighbour's line is never glued to the next, and a read-only file is left alone.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
version.changelog: Started by ReaKit FX - Start with REAPER, the panel opens to show Floatter is on and closes by itself after a few seconds; move the mouse over it, click or scroll in it to keep it open. Floatter keeps running either way. Its messages, such as a missing js_ReaScriptAPI, now show for that launch too. The panel shows the right version.

version.author: Quaz (EON Studios)
